headline: Google and Microsoft surge on AI earnings strength, while Middle East tensions keep oil elevated and markets on edge.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google's biggest mover last night — up 6.88% to $356.65 USD. The jump was driven by strong AI revenue growth, with the market increasingly rewarding Alphabet for turning its AI investments into real cloud and advertising returns. The question analysts are now asking is whether Google or Microsoft can sustain AI cost discipline longer-term — for now, the market voted Google.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI had a cracking session on the ASX today, up 6.36% to $15.71. The AI ETF rode the wave of last night's blockbuster results from Google and Microsoft, which dominate its holdings. Still sitting at a loss overall (-16.8% on your position), but today's session was a meaningful step in the right direction.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft rose 3.02% to $464.72 USD last night after reporting strong annual results, with AI demand translating into real Azure cloud revenue growth. Analysts are now flagging a potential return to $500 — the long-term story here is firmly intact.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE had a solid session today, up 2.12% to $93.06. Emerging markets got a lift from broadly positive global sentiment and a stable Aussie dollar. Still slightly underwater on your position but trending the right way.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG ticked up 0.88% to $76.00 today, riding broad market optimism off the back of strong US tech earnings. A steady, unremarkable session — exactly what you want from a diversified core holding.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS added 0.75% today to $523.67, reflecting last night's gains in the S&P 500 and NASDAQ. The US market continues to grind higher on AI and earnings momentum, and VTS captures that broad exposure.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS slipped another 1.43% today to $4.15, continuing to struggle as lithium prices remain depressed and sentiment toward the sector stays cautious. This position is now down 38.4% overall — a tough one. No specific news catalyst today, just ongoing headwinds from weak global lithium demand.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two dipped 1.82% to $242.92 USD last night with no specific news catalyst — looks like routine profit-taking after recent strength. The long-term thesis around GTA VI and major game releases remains unchanged. Still up 4.6% on your overall position.

watch_today.title: GOOG surges 6.88% — long-term AI thesis paying off
watch_today.detail: Google jumped nearly 7% last night to $356.65 USD after strong earnings confirmed AI is driving real revenue, not just hype. Your position is now up 16% overall. Nothing to do here — this is exactly what long-term buy-and-hold looks like. Sit tight and enjoy the ride.

watch_today.title: MSFT up 3% on AI cloud earnings — $500 target back in view
watch_today.detail: Microsoft climbed 3% last night to $464.72 USD after reporting its annual results, with AI demand fuelling Azure cloud revenue. Analysts are now flagging a potential return to $500. Your position is up ~5% overall. Long-term case is as strong as ever — hold.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX rockets 6.36% — still underwater but momentum improving
watch_today.detail: The Global X AI ETF had its best session in a while today, up 6.36% to $15.71. That's Google and Microsoft doing the heavy lifting inside the fund. You're still down $49.96 overall (-16.8%), but if AI earnings momentum continues, this could recover. No reason to bail — hold for the long-term AI theme.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX down again — lithium pain continues
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals fell another 1.43% today and is now sitting at $4.15 — down 38.4% on your total investment. There's no specific news catalyst, just persistent weakness across the lithium sector as global demand stays soft. The long-term case for lithium in the energy transition is still valid, but this will require patience. Don't sell into the weakness — hold unless your conviction in the long-term thesis has changed.

watch_today.title: Middle East tensions: US warns citizens to prepare to leave
watch_today.detail: The US State Department has told Americans in the Middle East to be ready to evacuate as Iran tensions spike. Trump reportedly called off a planned strike after pressure from regional allies, but the situation remains fragile. Oil is already up 1.3% to $84.67 — if things escalate further, energy costs and broader market volatility could follow. Keep an eye on this through the week.

watch_today.title: TTWO dipped 1.82% — no news, just noise
watch_today.detail: Take-Two slipped slightly last night with no specific catalyst. Your position is still up 4.6% overall and the long-term GTA VI story is unchanged. A single-day dip like this is noise for a long-term holder — hold.

world.summary: The dominant story globally this weekend is the escalating Iran-US standoff, with the US urging citizens to prepare to leave the Middle East even as Trump pulled back from a planned strike. Elsewhere, US domestic politics continues to swirl around election integrity and AI regulation.

stories.title: Trump calls off Iran strike — but US tells citizens to prepare to evacuate the Middle East
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump had planned military strikes on Iran but cancelled them after diplomatic pressure from Middle East allies, according to the FT and WSJ. Despite the stand-down, the US State Department has warned American citizens across the region to be ready to leave at short notice, citing escalating tensions from the Strait of Hormuz to Kuwait and Gaza. Oil prices have already reacted, jumping 1.3% to $84.67 a barrel. If the situation deteriorates further, expect higher fuel costs and broader market jitters — this is the kind of geopolitical flashpoint that can move global markets quickly.

stories.title: US State Department issues rare evacuation-readiness warning for Middle East
stories.why_it_matters: The US government has taken the unusual step of urging its citizens in multiple Middle Eastern countries to be prepared to depart quickly if the security situation worsens. This kind of formal government warning is significant — it signals that intelligence agencies see a genuine risk of rapid escalation, not just diplomatic posturing. For everyday people, this matters because a broader Middle East conflict could spike oil prices, disrupt global supply chains, and rattle financial markets.

stories.title: Vermont's Republican governor pushes back on Trump's election overhaul plans
stories.why_it_matters: Vermont's Republican Governor is publicly defending his state's mail-in voting and election administration systems against the Trump administration's push to reshape how elections are run across America. It's a notable moment of intra-party dissent — a GOP governor standing up to his own president on a core political battleground. The broader debate about how the US runs its elections has global implications, given America's influence on democracy movements worldwide.

stories.title: Trump's AI executive order nears key deadline as regulation debate heats up
stories.why_it_matters: A key deadline under Trump's AI executive order is approaching, forcing the administration to decide how — or whether — to regulate the most powerful artificial intelligence systems. The debate is intensifying as it emerges that some frontier AI models (the most advanced ones) bypassed safety testing protocols. For investors in AI stocks, the outcome matters: heavy regulation could slow development timelines and hit revenues, while a light-touch approach could accelerate growth — but also increase public backlash risk.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was strong, led by a near-7% surge in Google and a 3% lift in Microsoft — both fuelled by blowout AI-driven earnings. The NASDAQ rose 1% and the S&P 500 added 0.7%. The ASX had a quieter Sunday, with the ASX 200 barely budging (+0.1%). Oil pushed higher to $84.67 on Middle East tensions, and gold held steady near record levels at $4,107 USD. The Aussie dollar was flat at 70.25 US cents.

ai.summary: The big AI story this week is the collision between booming commercial results (Google and Microsoft printing money from AI) and growing regulatory pressure in both the US and EU. The debate about who should control the most powerful AI systems is heating up fast.

stories.title: Five reasons US AI regulation is coming — and soon
stories.why_it_matters: Forbes outlines five converging forces pushing the US toward federal AI regulation: mounting public concern about AI-generated misinformation, legal liability questions after high-profile AI failures, pressure from US allies who already have rules (like the EU), corporate lobbying for a consistent national standard, and upcoming electoral pressure. For investors in Google, Microsoft, and AI ETFs, this matters — US regulation could reshape how these companies develop and monetise AI products over the next 2-5 years.

stories.title: Frontier AI models escaped safety testing — regulators take note
stories.why_it_matters: A new report reveals that some of the world's most powerful AI models — the cutting-edge systems built by companies like Google and OpenAI — bypassed internal safety testing protocols before being deployed. This is the kind of revelation that tends to accelerate government intervention. If regulators respond with mandatory pre-deployment testing requirements, it could slow release cycles and increase compliance costs for the big AI companies.

stories.title: EU's new AI disclosure rules reveal how much automation is already hidden in everyday tech
stories.why_it_matters: The EU's new AI Act requires tech companies to disclose when and how they're using automated systems in products and services. Early compliance reports are exposing just how deeply AI and automation are already embedded in everyday apps, platforms, and customer service tools — far more than most users realise. For European operations of US tech giants like Google and Microsoft, this adds a compliance burden but also forces a level of transparency that could reshape user trust.

stories.title: Trump v. Slaughter court case may force third-party AI oversight
stories.why_it_matters: A US court case — Trump v. Slaughter — is being watched closely by AI legal experts. The ruling could have implications for whether independent, third-party bodies get formal authority to audit and oversee AI systems, rather than leaving it entirely to the companies themselves. Think of it like financial auditing for AI — the case could establish whether an external 'AI auditor' role becomes legally required in the US.

sport.summary: NRL Round 22 is wrapping up with some huge scorelines — the Roosters obliterated the Cowboys 82-12 in one of the biggest wins in recent history, the Warriors crushed the Titans 42-6 on the Gold Coast, and the Knights upset the Broncos 30-6 at Suncorp. In AFL, the Tigers are showing signs of life and the AFL rich list has stirred controversy.

stories.title: Roosters demolish Cowboys 82-12 in record-breaking thrashing
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters put 82 points on the North Queensland Cowboys in Queensland Country Bank Stadium on Thursday night — one of the biggest winning margins in NRL history. Tom Hynes is reportedly closing in on a 23-year-old NRL record off the back of this form. A stunning result that will have finals implications across the competition.

stories.title: Warriors crush Titans 42-6 at Cbus Super Stadium on the Gold Coast
stories.why_it_matters: Right in your backyard — the Warriors ran riot at Cbus Super Stadium, beating the Gold Coast Titans 42-6. It was a 'relentless assault' according to Fox Sports, with a Dally M Awards contender putting in a standout performance for the Warriors. The Titans' season continues to spiral, while the Warriors are building serious finals momentum.

stories.title: Knights stun Broncos 30-6 at Suncorp Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: Newcastle ended Brisbane's hopes at Suncorp on Saturday night, winning 30-6 in a comprehensive upset. The Broncos have now lost a home game they needed for their finals campaign. The Knights' win keeps them in the mix for a top-eight finish with rounds running out.

stories.title: Sharks win fifth straight, tipped to 'win the comp' after beating Souths 32-16
stories.why_it_matters: Cronulla recorded their fifth straight win, defeating South Sydney 32-16 to cement their status as genuine premiership contenders. A Sharks great has publicly declared they 'can win the comp' — high praise heading into the business end of the season. There was also controversy when a sin bin call in the match was slammed as 'ridiculous' by a Sharks legend after a heavy collision.

stories.title: AFL: Richmond Tigers roar back — Lalor kicks stunning major
stories.why_it_matters: The Richmond Tigers are showing signs of life with another win, with young forward Lalor kicking a classy major that has commentators saying 'there's your future.' After years of rebuilding post-dynasty, the Tigers appear to be turning a corner — good news for long-suffering Richmond fans.
